resources.string: Watches the YouTube app while you are viewing Shorts and swipes to the next Short for you when the current one finishes playing, so you can keep watching hands-free. It reads on-screen content only while the YouTube app is in the foreground, and nothing is ever recorded, stored or sent off the device.
Turn the service on in Android Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Shorts Auto Scroll.
Open YouTube Shorts and the app will swipe for you when a Short ends.
Master on/off. Also togglable from the Quick Settings tile or the floating bubble.
Smart — when the Short actually ends
Reads the Shorts progress bar and swipes the moment playback reaches the end (or loops back to the start). Falls back to the fixed timer if no progress bar can be read.
Always swipe after a set number of seconds.
If playback progress stops moving, the countdown is put on hold.
Do not scroll while comments are open
Holds off while the comment or share sheet is on screen.
A small draggable button over YouTube. Tap to pause/resume auto scroll. Needs the "display over other apps" permission.
Accessibility scroll action, gesture as fallback
The YouTube app was not found on this device.

This app drives the normal YouTube app through Android\'s accessibility APIs: it never signs in, never downloads video, and never talks to any server. If YouTube changes its layout the "Smart" detection may stop finding the progress bar — the Diagnostics screen shows exactly what is being read, and the fixed timer keeps working regardless.
